Task: Copy invite: a copy button for a team app that copies an invite link and confirms success.
decision: Press Copy invite, and the link is copied with a tagged key you can later revoke.
plan:
## Pitch

**Optical technician:** A copied invite link is a key cut and handed over. Once it leaves the clipboard, nobody knows where it went. Each copy should mint its own key, with a three-letter tag, a role and an expiry, and the key should hang on a ring where it can be revoked. A builder can reuse that pattern: mint, label, revoke.

**Braille transcriber:** Keep two layers apart. The link store is a plain array of `{code, role, expiry, revoked}`. The view only renders it. Then the confirmation says exactly what was copied, such as "Copied · K7Q · Member · 24 h". It reads the same with no colour and no screen.

**Weather forecaster:** I walked a copy button with keys only and marked three hesitations. The first was focus jumping away after copy. The second was a green tick with no words. The third was a silent failure when the clipboard was blocked. The person who receives the link never sees our UI, so the sender has to know what they sent.

**Captain Nemo:** Give it an instrument, a brass ring of key tags. Each tag carries a notch pattern by role: one notch for Member, two for Admin. The pattern is shape, so it reads in grey. Then set "Administrator · 30 d" in the tag and see whether it holds.

## Clash

**Braille transcriber:** Two options. A tag shows the code as text, or it shows code plus notch glyph. I back code plus glyph, with the word always present.

**Captain Nemo:** Glyph alone is cleaner. Beauty is fewer marks.

**Weather forecaster:** Glyph alone fails the first-time sender. I hesitated on it in the walkthrough. Keep the word.

**Optical technician:** The ring is better than a bare toast already. Now make sure revoke survives. A revoked tag stays on the ring, struck through, with "Revoked". It does not vanish.

**Captain Nemo:** Struck and kept. Then fix the tag width from "Administrator · 30 d" so the ring never reflows.

**Weather forecaster:** Clipboard blocked on file://. Then what.

**Braille transcriber:** Option one: select the link text in a field and say "Press Ctrl+C". Option two: show a Retry. I back option one, because it always works.

**Optical technician:** Agreed. Ship one ring and one button, and no settings page.

## Decision

Press Copy invite, and the link is copied with a tagged key you can later revoke.

Concept: Key Ring Invite

- **Optical technician:** Defines the reusable rule of mint, label and revoke. Also specifies that revoked tags stay visible, struck through and labelled "Revoked".
- **Braille transcriber:** Separates the link store from the rendered ring. Writes the confirmation string from store data only. Owns the blocked-clipboard fallback, a selected text field with "Press Ctrl+C".
- **Weather forecaster:** Runs a keys-only walkthrough and logs each hesitation. Keeps focus on Copy invite after copy. Announces the result once in a polite live region. Revoke buttons are reachable by Tab.
- **Captain Nemo:** Draws the brass key-tag ring in SVG with notch patterns by role: 1 for Member, 2 for Admin. Fixes the tag width from the label "Administrator · 30 d".

Initial screen is about 14 words: "Invite to Harbor", Role select, Expires select, "Copy invite", "No live links".

## Build notes

1. Create `index.html` with a single module script. Hold `links = []` in a store. `mint()` makes a 3-letter code and a sample URL `harbor.app/j/K7Q`. `navigator.clipboard.writeText` runs with a try/catch. On failure, focus a readonly input with the URL selected and show "Press Ctrl+C".
2. Render the ring from the store into a `role="list"`. Each tag is 200 px wide and shows code, role, expiry, notch glyph and a Revoke button. Revoke sets `revoked:true`, strikes the text and adds the word "Revoked". The status line reads `Copied · K7Q · Member · 24 h` in `aria-live="polite"`.
3. Test keys only: Tab, Enter, Space. Test the 320 px width and greyscale. Test the longest label "Administrator · 30 d". Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the tag drop is skipped. Reset clears the ring to "No live links".
